summary: Descendants, adoptees and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share, two thirds if permanently incapable of work. The country has no trust law and is not party to the Hague Trusts Convention. Law differs between the Federation, Republika Srpska and Brcko District.
reserved_share: Descendants, adoptees and spouse: 1/2 of the intestate share (2/3 if permanently unable to work); other heirs have narrower rights; Law on Inheritance of the Federation, art. 30 (Republika Srpska law is similar).
foreign_law_note: The 1982 Law on Conflict of Laws, still applied, makes the deceased's national law govern succession; immovables in Bosnia follow Bosnian law. There is no free choice of law.
trust_note: No trust law. Foundations exist under state and entity laws on associations and foundations, aimed at public benefit.
open_questions: Article numbers and fractions in the Federation, Republika Srpska and Brcko laws were not read in the primary texts.
Whether the 1982 conflict law has been replaced by a new private international law act.
Whether foundations may benefit a family.
